marks.gloss_en: אתיא אחל אחל: here 'this day I will begin [achel] to put the dread of you' (Deut 2:25, of Moshe), there 'this day I will begin [achel] to magnify you' (Josh 3:7, of Yehoshua) -- so the sun broke through for Moshe as for Yehoshua
אתיא תת תת: here 'I will begin to put [tet] the dread of you' (Deut 2:25), there 'on the day the Lord put [tet] the Amorites' (Josh 10:12)
בשלמא נקדימון בן גוריון — גמרא: Nakdimon's case is a received tradition (the story just told). Kind svara under protest: no support kind for a tradition.
יהושע — נמי קרא, דכתיב: וידם השמש (Josh 10:13). Kind svara under protest: no citation-grade support kind.
the baraita: the sun broke through for Moshe (one of three)
רבי יוחנן אמר, אתיא מגופיה דקרא: when did the nations tremble (Deut 2:25)? when the sun broke through for Moshe
R' Yochanan: 'who shall hear the report of you and tremble and be in anguish because of you' (Deut 2:25) -- when did they tremble and were in anguish? when the sun broke through for Moshe
Nakdimon's prayer: Master of the world, it is revealed and known before You that I did not act for my honour nor my father's house's, but for Yours, that water be available to the pilgrims
Nakdimon to the hegmon: give me the price of the excess water you owe me
Nakdimon's second prayer: Master of the world, make known that You have beloved ones in Your world
דאמר רבי שמואל בר נחמני אמר רבי יונתן -- the curse of Achiya (the reed) is better than Bilaam's blessing, so the reed verse is for a blessing
Rav: 'the Lord will smite Israel as the reed is shaken in the water' (1 Kgs 14:15) is for a blessing
Rav: 'Jerusalem became as a nidda among them' (Lam 1:17) is for a blessing
Rav Yehuda: 'she became as a widow' (Lam 1:1) is for a blessing
Rav Yehuda: 'I too have made you contemptible and base' (Mal 2:9) is for a blessing

Achiya cursed them with a reed: the reed stands in a place of water, its stock renews, its roots are many; all the winds cannot move it from its place -- it goes and comes with them, and when they subside it stands in its place
but Bilaam the wicked blessed them with a cedar, as it says 'as cedars by the water' (Num 24:6)
a person should always be soft as a reed
the mishnah: and likewise a city upon which rain did not fall, etc. (lemma)
